name: Deep Learning
description: Neural networks from a single neuron to transformers, trained hands-on in PyTorch.

nodes.name: Neural networks
nodes.desc: Neurons, layers and multilayer perceptrons; the forward pass and counting parameters.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe neurons, layers and multilayer perceptrons, compute a forward pass and count a network's parameters.

nodes.name: Activation functions
nodes.desc: Sigmoid, tanh, ReLU and friends, and why non-linearity matters.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare sigmoid, tanh, ReLU and related activations and explain why non-linearity is essential.

nodes.name: Loss functions
nodes.desc: Mean squared error, cross-entropy and softmax outputs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose and compute mean squared error, cross-entropy and softmax outputs for regression and classification.

nodes.name: Backpropagation
nodes.desc: Computing gradients with the chain rule over a computation graph, and automatic differentiation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute gradients with the chain rule over a computation graph and explain how automatic differentiation works.

nodes.name: Optimisers
nodes.desc: SGD with momentum, RMSProp, Adam and learning-rate schedules.
nodes.summary: You will be able to train networks with SGD, momentum, RMSProp and Adam and choose learning-rate schedules.

nodes.name: Init & normalisation
nodes.desc: Weight initialisation, vanishing and exploding gradients, batch and layer normalisation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to initialise weights sensibly, diagnose vanishing and exploding gradients and apply batch and layer normalisation.

nodes.name: Regularising nets
nodes.desc: Dropout, weight decay, data augmentation and early stopping.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reduce overfitting in neural networks with dropout, weight decay, data augmentation and early stopping.

nodes.name: Digit recogniser
nodes.desc: Train an MLP on MNIST in PyTorch, plot training curves, and tune the optimiser and regularisation.
nodes.summary: You will train an MLP on MNIST in PyTorch, plot its training curves and tune the optimiser and regularisation.

nodes.name: Convolutional nets
nodes.desc: Convolutions, padding and stride, pooling, and feature maps.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain convolutions, padding, stride and pooling and compute the size of the resulting feature maps.

nodes.name: CNN architectures
nodes.desc: LeNet, VGG and ResNet, residual connections and why depth helps.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe LeNet, VGG and ResNet and explain how residual connections make very deep networks trainable.

nodes.name: Transfer learning
nodes.desc: Fine-tuning pretrained networks and using them as feature extractors.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fine-tune pretrained networks and use them as fixed feature extractors for new tasks.

nodes.name: Image classifier
nodes.desc: Fine-tune a pretrained CNN on your own small image dataset and analyse its mistakes.
nodes.summary: You will fine-tune a pretrained CNN on your own small image dataset and analyse the mistakes it makes.

nodes.name: Recurrent nets
nodes.desc: Recurrent networks over sequences, backpropagation through time and its gradient problems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how recurrent networks process sequences, train them with backpropagation through time and recognise their gradient problems.

nodes.name: LSTM & GRU
nodes.desc: Gated recurrent units and long short-term memory cells.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how LSTM and GRU gates control information flow and help with long-range dependencies.

nodes.name: Word embeddings
nodes.desc: Tokenisation, embedding layers and word2vec-style representations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to tokenise text and represent tokens with embedding layers and word2vec-style vectors.

nodes.name: Text generator
nodes.desc: Train a character-level LSTM language model and sample text from it.
nodes.summary: You will train a character-level LSTM language model and sample new text from it using temperature.

nodes.name: Attention
nodes.desc: Query, key and value; scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute scaled dot-product attention with queries, keys and values and explain multi-head attention.

nodes.name: Transformers
nodes.desc: The transformer block, positional encodings, encoder versus decoder models.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe the transformer block, positional encodings and the difference between encoder and decoder models.

nodes.name: Pretrained LMs
nodes.desc: Pretraining and fine-tuning, BERT and GPT-style models, and prompting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain pretraining and fine-tuning of BERT and GPT-style language models and how prompting uses them.

nodes.name: Transformer fine-tune
nodes.desc: Fine-tune a small pretrained transformer for text classification and compare it with your LSTM.
nodes.summary: You will fine-tune a small pretrained transformer for text classification and compare its results with your LSTM model.

nodes.name: Autoencoders
nodes.desc: Autoencoders and variational autoencoders, latent spaces and reconstruction.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build autoencoders and variational autoencoders and explain latent spaces and reconstruction losses.

nodes.name: GANs
nodes.desc: Generator versus discriminator, adversarial training and its instabilities.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how a generator and discriminator are trained adversarially and why GAN training is unstable.

nodes.name: Diffusion models
nodes.desc: Denoising diffusion: the forward noising process and learning to reverse it.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain denoising diffusion models, from the forward noising process to learning the reverse denoising steps.
